top.title: ‘World-class’: Erik Spoelstra gives ‘the greatest compliment you could give’ to one Knicks star
top.description: Photo by Eric Espada/Getty Images Erik Spoelstra is widely regarded as one of the best coaches in the NBA. The 56-year-old has turned the Miami Heat’s season around by winning 11 of his side’s last 14 games after losing each of his first four. On Friday, Spoelstra secured another win, this time against the New York Knicks, but before the game, he lavished praise on the defending champions’ best player – Jalen Brunson. Erik Spoelstra says Jalen Brunson has ‘the heart of a champion’ Brunson is arguably the biggest reason why the New York Knicks won the NBA championship last season. The 30-year-old won the NBA Cup MVP, Eastern Conference Finals MVP and NBA Finals MVP awards as he led the Knicks to their first title in 53 years. Spoelstra has faced Brunson plenty of times over the years and even coached him for Team USA at the 2023 FIBA Men’s Basketball World Cup. Ahead of the game on Friday, the Heat coach raved about Brunson and what he has always felt about the Knicks superstar. He said, as per Jared Schwartz of the New York Post on X : “He has the heart of a champion and I think he’s had that for a long time. “The one thing, we faced him in the playoffs a few years ago, and you feel him as a competitor. And that’s probably the greatest compliment you could give him, is he’s a world-class, top-percentile competitor. “He transcends what his size may be, and he’s going to make you take note of him every single possession that he’s out on the court. And in the moments of truth, that’s probably when he showed up the biggest. I have respect for him as a competitor as much as I have for anyone in this league.” The Miami Heat ended up beating the New York Knicks on Friday, with Bam Adebayo and Giannis Antetokounmpo producing a combined 47 points and 30 rebounds. However, Brunson caused them plenty of problems, scoring 27 points and recording three rebounds, eight assists and three steals. He came close to tying the game in the end, but Davion Mitchell saved the day for the Heat. The Knicks are now 12-7 for the season, which is not awful, but they need to get a lot better to have a chance of repeating what they did in the last campaign. top.title: WWE faces backlash for Bronson Reed tribute using ‘AI-generated’ voice
top.description: The professional wrestling community was struck by tragedy on Friday night, with news that Jerinrmaine Haley, known under his ring name Bronson Reed, passed away suddenly at age 38 . According to a statement from WWE , he died due to “medical complications.” WWE announced the news shortly before SmackDown on Friday night, which forced the company to scramble to put together a pre-show tribute. The company also shared a tribute on social media , featuring the on-screen graphic shown on SmackDown , along with a voiceover that sounded like commentator Michael Cole. When the tribute dropped on social media, however, something was amiss, and fans immediately took to social media, accusing WWE of using an AI-generated voiceover. Several comments were calling out the company for its “disrespect” and lack of effort put into giving Reed the proper tribute. Incredibly dystopian,” one fan wrote. “ Just don’t do a voiceover if it’s that inconvenient .” Another added, “If not one of the 10 most abjectly evil things to be done in and/or by this company, an AI-voiced tribute video stands out as one of the most immediately upsetting and gross things this company’s ever done.” MORE: WWE Survivor Series 2026: Predictions and match card analysis Other fans were extremely disappointed in the lack of effort that went into Friday night’s tribute. top.title: Gunmen kill 51-year-old man, two others in fresh Plateau attack
top.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Gunmen have killed three persons in a fresh attack on Nkiedowro community in Teegbe District of Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State, throwing residents into mourning. The attack, which occurred on Friday night, claimed the lives of three Irigwe natives, bringing to 20 the number of Irigwe people reportedly killed within the week, according to the National Publicity Secretary of the Irigwe Youth Movement, Joseph Chudu Yonkpa. Yonkpa, who confirmed the killings in a statement made available to newsmen on Saturday, said the attackers launched two separate ambushes on the community. “Yesterday night, Fulani militias launched two separate ambushes at Nkiedowro, Teegbe District, killing three Irigwe natives,” he said. He identified the victims as Ngudo Kura, 51; Hosea Ishaya, 26; and Naomi Izeh, 22. “This makes it a total of 20 Irigwe people killed this week in an unprovoked manner,” Yonkpa added. He expressed condolences to the families of the victims and the entire Irigwe community, praying for the repose of the souls of the deceased. Our correspondent reports that the latest killings occurred barely two days after 17 persons were given a mass burial following an attack on the Tafi Gana community, also in Bassa Local Government Area. The development has heightened concerns over the security situation in the area, with residents reportedly apprehensive about possible further attacks. The Irigwe Youth Movement urged residents to remain vigilant and avoid movements that could expose them to danger. “We call on our people to intensify vigilance, avoid late-night and isolated movements, and report suspicious movements to the relevant authorities,” Yonkpa said. The group also appealed to security agencies to strengthen surveillance and take necessary measures to protect communities in the area. Efforts to get the reaction of security operatives were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. He got there in 2011, and left in December of 2021, under intense pressure from the fan base. After a brief interim stint by Danny Manning, Turgeon’s successor was Kevin Willard, who stayed for three years. top.title: Joe Burrow praises Colbie Young’s work ethic after first NFL touchdown
top.description: It was an ugly night all-around for the Cincinnati Bengals in Washington, though it did have some bright spots. The weather was part of the ugliness, but the manner in which the Cincinnati Bengals played on Monday Night Football was the remainder of said unsightliness. After slogging to a 10-0 lead, the Bengals appeared to be uninspired for the final two quarters of the game (maybe even more), letting a should-be win slip through their fingers—metaphorically and realistically speaking. Even so, there were a couple of bright spots on an otherwise disappointing evening. After the Commanders tied the game with just under 12 minutes remaining in the third quarter, Cincinnati’s offense was on the move for what would essentially be the last time in the game. Needing a score to try and pull away from Washington’s scrappy efforts, Joe Burrow found rookie Colbie Young for his first touchdown catch as an NFL receiver. Joe Burrow extending the play and finding Colbie Young in the end zone for his first career touchdown reception in the NFL. pic.twitter.com/LVab2j2UZO — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 24, 2026 It was a vintage Burrow play, as he rolled right when the play broke down and found Young in the corner of the end zone. It was a critical play at the time, as the team was largely struggling on offense, and the Bengals regained the lead at 17-10. That was Young’s only catch on two targets against Washington, and only his second on the 2026 season, but it was a gigantic one from an overall game perspective. The Bengals went on to lose, but Young proved to be a bright spot in an otherwise ugly night. And it could be the start of a bigger role moving forward. During his weekly press conference, Burrow made sure to point out Young’s work ethic as part of why he’s growing into his role within the offense. “Seems to never make the same mistake twice. Works hard to be better,” Burrow said of Young. The rookie wide receiver has seen increased snaps with Andrei Iosivas still sitting on injured reserve. And, like Iosivas, Young is in that third receiver role that attempts to clear out space for Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, while also being a blocker in the run game, and occasionally being called upon in the explosive offense. While he’s still growing in the role, this first touchdown reception gives optimism about his development. When the Bengals drafted him in the third round this year, they knew that he was a height/weight/speed/athleticism specimen who could stretch the field but needed polish. The fact that Young’s touchdown reception was a short-yardage one in the red zone on a broken play should catch the attention of the staff. We will see how that ends up translating down the stretch.

top.description: Borussia Mönchengladbach supporters carry on with ‘bingo card’ protest against kickoff times Borussia Mönchengladbach supporters are carrying on with their “bingo” protest against 2026/27 Bundesliga fixture scheduling, culminating in a brief interruption during Friday evening’s 3-3 draw against Werder Bremen. The latest demonstration follows weeks of complaints about inconvenient kick-off times, with Gladbach supporters previously introducing a satirical campaign dubbed “Ansetzungs-Bullshit-Bingo” (fixture-scheduling bullshit bingo). The protests centre on the German Football League’s (DFL) decision to schedule three of Gladbach’s longest away journeys on Friday evenings within the space of just over a month. Matches against VfB Stuttgart, Hamburger SV, and Werder Bremen were all assigned 20:30 kick-offs, creating considerable logistical difficulties for travelling supporters. Gladbach supporters protest against three Friday-night away fixtures Friday’s encounter at the Weserstadion was temporarily interrupted in the 49th minute after golf balls were thrown onto the playing surface from the Gladbach away section. Referee Felix Zwayer briefly halted proceedings while the objects were cleared. The demonstration followed Franck Honorat’s goal shortly after halftime, which had given Gladbach a 2-1 lead. The visitors subsequently extended their advantage to 3-1 before conceding twice in the closing stages, with Niclas Füllkrug rescuing a point for Bremen in stoppage time. The underlying grievance had been apparent since September, when the DFL announced the precise kick-off times for matchdays five through eleven. Supporters wishing to attend all three fixtures in Stuttgart, Hamburg, and Bremen faced approximately 2,350 kilometres of return travel. Each journey involved hundreds of kilometres on a working day, with many fans potentially forced to take time off, leave work early, or arrange overnight accommodation. The first of those fixtures took place at Stuttgart’s MHPArena on October 23. Get German Football News was present for Gladbach’s dramatic 3-2 victory over Stuttgart. The Gladbach fans first raised their bingo card at this fixture. German football magazine 11FREUNDE subsequently highlighted their protest in its regular Kurvenschau examination of German fan culture, emphasizing the inconvenience of requiring supporters to travel more than 400 kilometres to Stuttgart on a Friday. The bingo concept turned the seemingly endless frustrations surrounding Bundesliga scheduling into a satirical protest, with supporters using the language of a familiar game to draw attention to kick-off arrangements they considered increasingly unreasonable. The campaign reflected a grievance that long predates the current season. top.title: INEC Declares Readiness For 2027, Expresses Satisfaction With Plateau Mock Election
top.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has declared its readiness for the 2027 general elections, assuring Nigerians that it is committed to conducting free, inclusive, credible and transparent polls. INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, gave the assurance while monitoring Saturday’s mock election in Plateau State, where he expressed satisfaction with the turnout of voters and the conduct of the exercise. Amupitan said the mock election was designed to test the functionality of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV), as well as assess the efficiency of the accreditation process ahead of the 2027 general elections. INEC Chairman Amupitan inspecting the exercise in Jos on Saturday, November 28, 2026. He commended voters for their orderly conduct, expressing delight at seeing an elderly woman turn out for the exercise and successfully undergo accreditation. “You can see yourself that the turnout is very good. What we are trying to test is actually the working of the machines, which are the BVAS and the IReV, and voters are being accredited. You can see how orderly it is going. From what we have seen, I am impressed,” he said. The INEC chairman acknowledged the support of the Plateau State Independent Electoral Commission in mobilising residents for the exercise but noted that the environmental sanitation exercise earlier scheduled for Saturday may have affected early participation, as some residents had indicated they would be unable to come out in time. On the commission’s preparedness for the 2027 elections, Amupitan said INEC was determined to deliver one of the best elections in the country’s history. “For the 2027 general elections, INEC is prepared, and I want to assure all Nigerians that we are going to have one of the best elections. We are determined that the 2027 election will be free, inclusive, credible and transparent,” he stated. Addressing concerns over the security situation in the country, the INEC chairman said the commission was working with relevant security agencies to ensure the protection of voters and electoral personnel during the forthcoming elections. He disclosed that INEC recently convened a one-day national security conference where stakeholders deliberated on security challenges and measures to safeguard the electoral process. Amupitan further revealed that the commission had conducted a risk assessment of polling units across the country, with identified locations shared with law enforcement agencies to enable them to strengthen security arrangements ahead of the elections. “We have done what we call a risk assessment of all the polling units in Nigeria, and we have identified all the polling units and shared them with the law enforcement agencies so that they can make extra preparations ahead of the elections,” he said. top.title: Red Sox Floated as Potential Landing Spot for Former No. 1 Overall Pick
top.description: Red Sox Floated as Potential Landing Spot for Former No. 1 Overall Pick originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Reports indicate the Red Sox are still looking to improve on the mound this offseason, and among the options that make sense, going after a former No. 1 overall pick could be at the top of that list. Casey Mize, the Padres free agent, has been very impressive over the past few years. There have been moments when Mize has been a bit disappointing because of the injuries that he's dealt with, and in 2026, in the second half for San Diego, he posted a 7.46 ERA, but what I'm looking at is that 2.70 ERA he posted in 16 starts for the Tigers in the first half. Ian Browne of MLB.com believes he could be an option for the Red Sox, adding that he fits exactly what Craig Breslow could be looking for. "After a strong 16-start sample last season for the Tigers (2.70 ERA), Mize faded after the Trade Deadline deal that sent him to the Padres, as evidenced by a 7.46 ERA in 10 starts. The ERA was inflated by two rough outings. "He gave up eight runs in 3 1/3 innings in his first start for the Padres at Arizona on Aug. 5 and gave up a seven-spot in four innings in his final start of the regular season on Sept. 25 -- again against the D-backs. However, health contributed to Mize's late-season slide. He slipped on the dugout steps in August and ended the season on the 15-day injured list with a right ankle sprain. Breslow likes extension with his pitchers, and Mize was in the 83rd percentile in that department in '26," Browne wrote . The impressive first half with Detroit shows what Mize can do when things are right. The struggles in San Diego, as Browne pointed out, might not have been as bad as they make it seem in his numbers because of a couple of bad starts. What I was a bit worried about with Mize is that he only struck out 25 hitters in 44.2 innings. Not to say that he's a big swing-and-miss guy, never striking out more than 139 hitters in a season, but he has the stuff to get outs. He feels like a guy who might have to take a one- or two-year deal to raise his value. If that ends up being the case, it would make a lot of sense for the Red Sox to have some level of interest in him. top.title: Celtics Insider Throws Shade at Jayson Tatum for Jaylen Brown Reason
top.description: Celtics Insider Throws Shade at Jayson Tatum for Jaylen Brown Reason originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Celtics look very different from how they did a year ago, a couple of seasons ago, and all in between. Typically, we're used to seeing the Celtics be one of the best teams in the NBA. While Boston hasn't been terrible this year, sitting at 12-7, it's not unfair to say it's been somewhat disappointing, at least over the past week and a half. When Boston decided to move on from Jaylen Brown in a deal to land Paul George, it was always going to lead to ridiculous takes about Jayson Tatum not being the best player on the roster since he entered the league. That's continued to be the case, and Sherrod Blakely was the latest one to bring it up, adding that he doesn't believe that Tatum can play with this roster because it's not good enough, but Brown was able to a year ago. "This [team] is the Transformer that was made out of bits and pieces of sh*t that people didn't want...Jaylen can work with that...[Tatum] needs better players around him to be a great player,” Sherrod Blakely said . Without a doubt, the Celtics had a nice regular season last year, going 56-26 and finishing in second place in the Eastern Conference. Brown was very good last season as well, but there should also be some context added. There were multiple players on the Celtics who stepped up in a big way last year, including Payton Pritchard, who averaged 17 points and shot 37.7% from 3-point range. Whether people want to say that was because of what Brown can do for his teammates, that's one thing, but Pritchard hasn't been the same player this year, averaging just 12.8 points per game and shooting 33.6% from the field. As I've said before, I see this more as an issue with the Celtics as a whole not playing good basketball instead of just blaming Tatum, who admittedly hasn't played as well as we're used to seeing him, but it's also not ridiculous considering that he’s still working back from a very difficult injury to come back from. top.title: Real Madrid’s 17-year-old defensive gem shines at U17 World Cup after switching Spain for France
top.description: Real Madrid’s 17-year-old defensive gem shines at U17 World Cup after switching Spain for France Real Madrid’s next generation is beginning to take shape, with the academy producing a number of gems who have genuine first-team prospects. Los Blancos have placed a lot of emphasis on developing talent in the academy, even if not all players go on to make it to the first team. While players like Thiago Pitarch earn first-team opportunities at the Santiago Bernabeu , others, like Nico Paz and Jacobo Ramon, are sold for significant sums. Now, according to MARCA , another Los Blancos academy prospect, Leo Lemaitre, has been one of the standout defenders at the U-17 World Cup in Qatar. The teenager switched allegiance to represent France rather than Spain and has impressed at the tournament. Leo Lemaitre impressing with France Lemaitre joined Real Madrid at 12 and has steadily climbed through the ranks at La Fabrica over the years. View this post on Instagram A post shared by @leolemaxx He signed a contract extension until 2028 in January and trained with Castilla during pre-season. He has since become part of the Juvenil A set-up. Having made six appearances for Spain’s U-15s and two for the U-16s, the teenager has now switched allegiance to France. His French father, Nicolas, explained that the family maintained close ties to the country, prompting Leo to make the switch. France Under-17 coach Jose Alcocer admitted that the youngster had been difficult to identify because he played outside France and had previously used his mother’s surname. However, the decision already seems to be paying off, with Leo forming an excellent partnership with Mohamed Sylla. Real Madrid have another promising defensive talent The 17-year-old’s numbers in the tournament have been impressive. He is averaging 7.87 ball recoveries per match. top.description: Five of the Premier League's greatest loan cult heroes Football fans are told never to fall in love with a loan player. But when a temporary transfer produces performances of such quality, it's almost impossible for them not to win hearts. Ronald Araujo is the latest loanee to become a fan favourite, with the defender earning Anfield admiration at Liverpool. Should the Reds opt against a permanent deal, Araujo could join the long list of Premier League loan cult heroes. Carlos Tevez - West Ham Carlos Tevez 's move to West Ham remains one of the most infamous deals in Premier League history. West Ham's shock swoop for the Argentine forward and compatriot Javier Mascherano stunned football, as two of world football's best up-and-coming talents headed to the East End. While Mascherano muddled through a forgettable six months before leaving, Tevez dug deep to make an impact. After a slow start, the forward's form caught fire. He scored his first goal in March, and ended the season with seven goals in nine games. West Ham had been 10 points from safety in early March, but a remarkable run carried the club to safety. Tevez's winner at Manchester United on the final day confirmed Premier League status, and cemented him as a West Ham hero. However, the deal proved controversial. West Ham were found to have breached third-party ownership regulations, with the rights to both Tevez and Mascherano partially held by agent Kia Joorabchian's company, Media Sports Investment (MSI). A messy fallout followed, with Sheffield United, who were relegated at West Ham's expense, eventually receiving £20m in an out-of-court settlement in 2009. Henrik Larsson - Manchester United Manchester United signed Henrik Larsson on a short-term loan deal in 2007, as the Swedish striker arrived to add depth to Sir Alex Ferguson's squad. top.title: NFL fans divided over what Jason Whitlock has said about Aaron Rodgers after Steelers game
top.description: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images The post-Aaron Rodgers era got off to a surprisingly positive start for the Pittsburgh Steelers, who secured a win over the previously 8-2 Denver Broncos on Friday night. Mason Rudolph is the man tasked with filling Rodgers’ boots and despite not playing 10 or more games in a season since 2019, he played fairly well during the Week 12 action. The Steelers ended up winning 27-5 and on the back of that victory, Jason Whitlock took to X to say that the veteran quarterback made the ‘ultimate sacrifice for his teammates’ and ‘took the bullet to improve the Steelers’. top.title: Why The NBA’s New Draft Lottery Could Cripple The Trade Deadline
top.description: NBA Deputy Commissioner Mark Tatum announces that the Chicago Bulls had won the seventh pick during the NBA basketball draft lottery Tuesday, May 14, 2019, in Chicago. (AP Photo/Nuccio DiNuzzo) Copyright 2019 The Associated Press. All rights reserved The NBA’s February trade deadline has become an annual holiday for basketball fans. It’s the last chance for teams to make blockbuster additions that can upend the championship picture. However, the trade deadline may be a casualty of the NBA’s new draft lottery. In an effort to deter teams from tanking, the league completely overhauled its lottery system this past May. Previously, the teams with the three worst records all had a 14.0% chance of landing the No. 1 overall pick, and no team could fall more than four spots from where they finished in the standings. That’s no longer the case. Under the new lottery, the teams with three worst records have worse odds than the other seven teams that miss the play-in tournament. Those teams can now fall as low as the 12th overall pick, while the other 13 teams in the lottery—which includes the losers of the No. 7 vs. No. 8 play-in game—can drop as far as 16th. That’s not all. Teams are now prohibited from landing the No. 1 overall pick in back-to-back drafts via the lottery. They also can’t receive top-five picks in three straight years. While the new lottery might not completely dissuade teams from tanking, it should at least prevent the egregious shenanigans that have been on full display late in the past few seasons. However, the decreased odds for the teams in the so-called “relegation zone” could also deter teams from embarking upon trade-deadline teardowns, even if that would otherwise be in their best long-term interests. “There will be less sellers than ever before,” one Eastern Conference team strategist told Jake Fischer of The Stein Line in mid-November. That doesn’t mean this year’s trade deadline will be a complete bust. In fact, a few teams are uniquely equipped to ignore the new lottery system and tear down with impunity. But teams that do control their own 2027 first-round pick will have to think twice before taking a stick of dynamite to their roster at this year’s trade deadline. Which Would-Be Sellers Might Stand Pat? If the previous lottery system were still in place, the Sacramento Kings might be the NBA’s most obvious seller at this year’s trade deadline. At 2-16, the Kings are already 7.5 games behind the 10th-seeded Oklahoma City Thunder for the final spot in the West’s play-in tournament. nigeria.title: Gunmen kill 51-year-old man, two others in fresh Plateau attack
nigeria.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Gunmen have killed three persons in a fresh attack on Nkiedowro community in Teegbe District of Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State, throwing residents into mourning. The attack, which occurred on Friday night, claimed the lives of three Irigwe natives, bringing to 20 the number of Irigwe people reportedly killed within the week, according to the National Publicity Secretary of the Irigwe Youth Movement, Joseph Chudu Yonkpa. Yonkpa, who confirmed the killings in a statement made available to newsmen on Saturday, said the attackers launched two separate ambushes on the community. “Yesterday night, Fulani militias launched two separate ambushes at Nkiedowro, Teegbe District, killing three Irigwe natives,” he said. He identified the victims as Ngudo Kura, 51; Hosea Ishaya, 26; and Naomi Izeh, 22. “This makes it a total of 20 Irigwe people killed this week in an unprovoked manner,” Yonkpa added. He expressed condolences to the families of the victims and the entire Irigwe community, praying for the repose of the souls of the deceased. Our correspondent reports that the latest killings occurred barely two days after 17 persons were given a mass burial following an attack on the Tafi Gana community, also in Bassa Local Government Area. The development has heightened concerns over the security situation in the area, with residents reportedly apprehensive about possible further attacks. The Irigwe Youth Movement urged residents to remain vigilant and avoid movements that could expose them to danger. “We call on our people to intensify vigilance, avoid late-night and isolated movements, and report suspicious movements to the relevant authorities,” Yonkpa said. The group also appealed to security agencies to strengthen surveillance and take necessary measures to protect communities in the area. Efforts to get the reaction of security operatives were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. nigeria.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has declared its readiness for the 2027 general elections, assuring Nigerians that it is committed to conducting free, inclusive, credible and transparent polls. INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, gave the assurance while monitoring Saturday’s mock election in Plateau State, where he expressed satisfaction with the turnout of voters and the conduct of the exercise. Amupitan said the mock election was designed to test the functionality of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV), as well as assess the efficiency of the accreditation process ahead of the 2027 general elections. What we are trying to test is actually the working of the machines, which are the BVAS and the IReV, and voters are being accredited. You can see how orderly it is going. From what we have seen, I am impressed,” he said. The INEC chairman acknowledged the support of the Plateau State Independent Electoral Commission in mobilising residents for the exercise but noted that the environmental sanitation exercise earlier scheduled for Saturday may have affected early participation, as some residents had indicated they would be unable to come out in time. nigeria.title: Numbers ‘Impressive’ As Voters Turnout For INEC Mock Exercise In Kano
nigeria.description: The mock accreditation for the 2027 general elections is underway in Paniso ward, Kano, as voters were seen turning out in seemingly impressive numbers for the exercise, compared to other regions in the country. Our correspondent, who monitored one of the selected polling units, noted that two INEC staff and two ad hoc personnel are testing the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices. Although voter turnout is still relatively low as against what is expected, the exercise is progressing smoothly, with no discrepancies reported and the BVAS thumbprint verification functioning as expected so far. Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Joash Amupitan, is currently in Jos to inspect the ongoing mock accreditation exercise, ahead of the 2027 general elections. It’s about seven weeks before the 2027 general election, and INEC is today running a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). Professor Joash Amupitan, INEC Chairman, disclosed this at the INEC and Office of the National Security Adviser ONSA) Strategic Election Security Conference in Abuja on Thursday. According to him, the exercise would put the Commission’s new equipment and result systems under live conditions. “While this exercise allows INEC to stress-test our upgraded BVAS devices and verify our stricter INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) validation safeguards—which automatically block arithmetic inconsistencies and over-voting, it also serves as an essential live dry run for our security architecture,” he said. nigeria.title: Kano varsity bans students, lecturers from exchanging gifts
nigeria.description: Northwest University, Kano, has prohibited students and lecturers from giving or receiving gifts in connection with university services, warning that anyone who violates the directive will face disciplinary action. The university classified the practice as corruption and serious misconduct, stressing that the ban applies to both staff and students, irrespective of the intentions behind the gifts. The Registrar, Isyaku Adamu, announced the directive in a statement issued on Friday, following public attention generated by reports of students presenting gifts to lecturers recognised as the best level coordinators or lecturers in their respective categories. According to the registrar, the practice could damage the institution’s reputation and violate provisions of its Service Conditions and Regulations (2025), as amended. The university specifically identified the giving and receiving of gifts as acts of corruption and conduct capable of bringing the institution into disrepute. “Consequently, any staff or students found involved in giving and/or receiving gift items for university services rendered will be charged with committing an act(s) of serious misconduct and the university will immediately initiate disciplinary process against the staff or students according to the university’s regulations,” Adamu said. He added that offenders would be liable to sanctions under Section 16 of the regulations. The registrar consequently urged members of the university community to observe the institution’s rules, ethical standards and best practices to avoid disciplinary action. He also called on staff and students to take the directive seriously, adding, “A stitch in time saves nine!” Northwest University, Kano, is a state-owned institution established by the Kano State Government in 2012. The incident followed the display of a pro-Palestinian banner bearing the inscription, “Revolt against the occupation, freedom for Palestine”, alongside Palestinian flags and chants against Israel. UEFA said the incidents contradicted its commitment to ensuring that football matches are played in an atmosphere of peace, mutual respect and sporting fairness. “The events witnessed at the above-mentioned matches run counter… to UEFA’s objective, enshrined in its Statutes, of ensuring that football matches are played in a spirit of peace, mutual respect and sporting fairness,” the governing body said. It added that it had appointed Ethics and Disciplinary Inspectors to investigate the incidents. The Besiktas fixture was moved from Istanbul to Georgia after Turkish authorities informed UEFA that the match could not be hosted in Turkey for safety and security reasons. nigeria.title: Pete Edochie: Linc breaks down in tears as unusual calm rules Enugu residence
nigeria.description: By Benjamin Njoku & By Dennis Agbo Linc Edochie, the third son of the late Pete Edochie, could not hold back his tears when he saw his father’s corpse in the mortuary. The movie legend died in the early hours of Wednesday after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. He had taken ill and was rushed to a hospital in Enugu, where he passed away. Painting a gloomy picture of the atmosphere at the late actor’s riverside residence in Trans-Ekulu, Enugu-based actor and filmmaker, Steve Eboh, said Linc broke down the moment he sighted his father’s body. “When Linc stormed the mortuary and sighted his father’s corpse, he cried profusely and leaned on his brother’s shoulder. We consoled him and prayed for the family,” Eboh said. Eboh added that grief was written all over the faces of people whose lives Pete Edochie had touched during his acting career. “We thank God for a life well spent. He was a legend who touched so many lives. He was not just an actor, he was a global icon. Everybody knew him.” Our correspondent, who visited the late actor’s Trans-Ekulu residence, described a gloomy picture of desertion and sorrow. “Apart from a domestic aide seen at the premises, there was little indication of the tragic development that had thrown the family and the Nigerian entertainment industry into mourning,” he noted. A source familiar with the circumstances surrounding his death told our correspondent that the actor took ill on Tuesday night and was subsequently rushed to a hospital in Enugu, where he died at about 12:30am on Wednesday. According to the source, Edochie’s family had remained at the hospital since his death, apparently attending to necessary arrangements and coming to terms with the loss. Picasso, whose real name is Piriye Isokrari said their previous deal gave Burna Boy 60 per cent, while the label took 40 per cent. He also revealed that the singer’s mother insisted he should only sign two-year contracts, a condition that influenced the label’s decision. According to Picasso, the proposed increase did not make financial sense at the time because the label was not making significant money from record sales. Picasso said live performances and endorsement deals were the major sources of revenue. He argued that accepting an 80-20 or 85-15 split would have left the label with a smaller share of the income despite the money it was investing in the singer. Picasso said the arrangement was difficult to justify for another two-year contract, particularly because the label was not entering a long-term deal. However, he admitted that his position has changed, saying he would now accept the terms he previously rejected. “Today I will take the 85/15 per cent now, but back then, it didn’t make any sense,” he said. nigeria.title: Chelsea in a ‘difficult moment’ admits Alonso
nigeria.description: Xabi Alonso admitted Chelsea are in a “difficult moment” as the beleaguered boss urged his struggling side to stick together after their dismal 3-2 defeat at Nottingham Forest on Friday. Alonso’s side crashed to a third successive Premier League loss to leave them languishing in eighth place. The Blues have lost four of their last five league matches, piling pressure on Alonso just months into his reign at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea fell behind to Igor Jesus’s early opener before Morgan Gibbs-White doubled Forest’s lead with a second half penalty. Emmanuel Emegha reduced the deficit but Gibbs-White struck again to make Emega’s late second nothing more than a footnote on another dispiriting evening for Alonso. “It’s a difficult moment for everyone. It’s disappointing again to lose again but we need to keep trying to find solutions, we can’t stop,” Alonso said. “We are low in confidence, the team is struggling to hold a result. After getting to 2-1 we have conceded and go to 3-1. “Everything is not going our way, we are responsible for that and we are responsible to find solutions.” Chelsea have already conceded 23 goals in 12 league matches and their porous defence was not helped by Alonso’s curious decision to use Ecuador midfielder Moises Caicedo in a back-three. Alonso also selected Wesley Fofana after the centre-back was forced to apologise for joking in a YouTube interview about missing a penalty during Chelsea’s League Cup defeat against Liverpool this season. The hapless Fofana was booed by angry Chelsea fans at the City Ground and conceded a penalty with his careless foul on former Blues striker Liam Delap. “We need to support everyone. Everyone that is in the team we need to support,” Alonso said of Fofana. “We know we have to go through difficult moments. We don’t take apart anyone and we want to help.” Asked to assess Chelsea’s dismal run, Alonso suggested the only cure was hard work on the training ground. “We can do better for sure. nigeria.title: Amotekun arrests suspect over alleged 200 house break-ins in Ondo
nigeria.description: …Over 200 master keys recovered from suspect By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Ondo State Security Network Agency, Amotekun Corps, has arrested a suspected serial housebreaker, identified as Michael Morayo, for allegedly breaking into more than 200 houses across different parts of the state. Morayo was among 13 suspected criminals paraded by the security outfit in Akure, the state capital. He was reportedly arrested in the Ijomu area of Akure. According to the Amotekun Corps, the suspect allegedly operated alone for about six years, breaking into houses and stealing household items, which he subsequently sold through an online marketplace he reportedly established. The security outfit said the suspect maintained an affluent lifestyle, dressed elegantly and spoke politely, making it difficult for people to suspect his alleged criminal activities. It added that he operated a warehouse where he kept stolen items and was meticulous in carrying out his operations. Parading the suspects, the State Commander of Amotekun, Chief Adetunji Adeleye, said Morayo allegedly confessed to breaking into more than 200 houses. Adeleye disclosed that over 200 master keys were recovered from him, explaining that the suspect often gained access to houses without forcing doors or breaking locks. “He does not always break doors to gain access to houses. We recovered well over 200 master keys from him. He also confessed that he usually finds ways of visiting people under different pretences. “In the process, he checks their doors and, while engaging them in conversation, removes one of their spare keys,” Adeleye said. He advised residents against keeping multiple keys in their door locks, warning that the practice could expose their homes to burglars. According to him, the suspect sometimes allegedly removed keys from doors and kept them in his pocket to gain access to the houses later. Adeleye further alleged that Morayo had other methods of gaining entry into homes, including making occupants fall asleep before stealing household equipment. The Amotekun commander said the suspect’s lifestyle and manner of presentation often shielded him from suspicion. He assured that all 13 suspects arrested and paraded by the corps would face prosecution after investigations. “After detailed investigations, they will be charged before courts of competent jurisdiction, depending on the offences they are suspected to have committed,” he said. nigeria.title: Plateau will overcome insecurity, says Jonathan
nigeria.description: …Hails Mutfwang’s unity initiative By Golok Nanmwa JOS — Former President Goodluck Ebele Jonathan has expressed optimism that Plateau State will overcome its lingering security challenges, describing the annual Plateau Unity Christmas Carols and Praise Festival as an important platform for reconciliation, peaceful coexistence and lasting peace. Jonathan, who commended Governor Caleb Manasseh Mutfwang for promoting unity through the annual religious gathering, spoke on Friday night at the third edition of the festival held at the Ten Commandments Prayer Altar, Jos. The festival, which began on November 27, 2026, brought together Christian leaders, traditional rulers, choristers, government officials and worshippers from within and outside the state to celebrate Christmas and promote unity among residents. The former president acknowledged the security challenges Plateau had experienced over the years but expressed confidence that the unity being promoted through the festival would help address divisions and strengthen relationships among communities. He commended the state government for sustaining the initiative, describing it as an important platform for bringing people together through worship and shared values. Jonathan also expressed confidence in Mutfwang’s commitment to promoting unity, while praying for divine intervention and the restoration of lasting peace in the state. He equally applauded former Governor Jonah David Jang for his contributions to leadership in Plateau State. Earlier, Mutfwang described the festival as a divine initiative established three years ago to unite the people under the banner of God, stressing that unity was essential to overcoming the challenges confronting the state. Declaring the event open, the governor expressed confidence in God’s protection, saying that despite the forces working against Plateau, the people would not be overwhelmed. He said: “If it were left to the forces that are arrayed against Plateau, we will not be gathered here tonight. But God has told us in His word that we will pass through the fires, we will not be consumed. We will pass through the waters, we will not be overwhelmed.” Mutfwang explained that the festival was conceived not merely as a musical celebration but as an opportunity for spiritual renewal, reconciliation and the removal of barriers to unity among residents. A small number of networks remain paused for maintenance, which Binance called standard practice and said was unrelated to the hack. The update closes out a month of phased reopenings. Binance confirmed the breach on Oct. 29, saying its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container, which was then used to submit unauthorized withdrawals. The world’s largest crypto exchange stopped all customer withdrawals for two days after the theft, Reuters reported . When they first reopened, customers pulled a net $4.7 billion off the platform, Binance said on Nov. 2. Binance covered the losses Binance said on Nov. 12 that it had completed coverage of the affected assets with more than $6.34 billion of company funds. The money came from a partial draw on its Secure Asset Fund for Users, part of its futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury, and the exchange pledged to rebuild SAFU to about $1 billion. Coverage is not the same as recovery. Binance replaced the stolen tokens from its own books, while about $2.85 billion of the stolen funds have been frozen remotely by the companies that issue them. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test Russian bank VTB began letting brokerage clients buy and sell bitcoin in its investing app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every Russian crypto buyer now has to pass. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later. The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. When retail buying became legal on Nov. 17 , T-Bank said it was waiting on a market standard for testing, and VTB said it was waiting on the remaining rules. Under the broker standard, the industry’s self-regulatory organization has three working days after publication to send brokers the answer options and correct answers. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders A New York judge has ordered the founders of NovaTech, a cryptocurrency investment scheme that targeted Haitian communities, to pay more than $1.37 billion, closing out the state’s case against a couple who fled the country rather than answer it. Justice Anar Rathod Patel of the New York County Supreme Court signed the order on Nov. 24. It holds Cynthia and Eddy Petion and their companies NovaTech Ltd, NovaTech Advisors and NovaPay jointly liable for $1,367,023,585 in disgorgement and interest. New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the win on Wednesday. “Today’s historic judgment finally delivers some semblance of justice for the thousands of New Yorkers who were targeted by this merciless scam,” James said. “NovaTech cruelly targeted immigrant families through faith and community groups with the promise of a better life while robbing them of their life savings.” Where the $1.37 billion figure comes from The award matches what the attorney general’s office asked for in October . The figure starts with the cryptocurrency investors sent to NovaTech’s wallet at payment processor CoinPayments, which totaled about $1.16 billion from August 2019 through May 2023, according to an affirmation filed by the state. Prosecutors subtracted the roughly $26 million NovaTech actually moved to its trading platform, leaving $1.13 billion in principal. Nine percent annual interest from June 2023 through September 2025 added another $232.5 million. NovaTech’s traders lost about $18.2 million of the money they did trade, the filing said. Everything else paid out of the wallet, including so-called returns and recruitment bonuses, came from other investors’ deposits. Cynthia Petion was the only authorized user on the CoinPayments account, and the state says she approved at least $134.5 million in crypto withdrawals to wallets belonging to her and her husband. The judge also ordered the Petions’ earlier venture, AWS Mining, to pay about $1.46 million. Cynthia Petion owes a separate $4.69 million tied to her promotion of that scheme. A NovaTech scheme built on prayer groups AWS Mining sold crypto mining contracts and promised 15% to 20% monthly returns before it collapsed in 2019, according to the attorney general’s office. The Petions then launched NovaTech, falsely marketed it as a registered hedge fund broker and advertised trading profits of about 2% to 4% a week. Promoters recruited through prayer groups, WhatsApp chats and ads in Haitian Creole. NovaTech collapsed in May 2023, and tens of thousands of investors couldn’t withdraw their crypto. The state sued in June 2024. The Petions never answered the complaint. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. But land, the asset our parents spoke about with the most respect, has no manual. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. A prospect once told me she had gone through my Instagram page carefully before she agreed to speak with me. She was checking whether I was consistent, whether my posts matched what I said on the phone, whether I had been around long enough to be real. I was flattered. Then I was worried. Because if a social media page has become part of a buyer’s due diligence, then a polished page has also become one of the easiest ways to deceive her. Instagram cannot tell you who owns a piece of land. Only a search at the land registry, done by your own lawyer, can begin to tell you that. Instagram cannot tell you whether a plot sits under government acquisition or on a planned road. A surveyor who charts the coordinates and checks them against official maps can. No number of testimonials replaces a written contract that states what you are paying for, what you are not paying for, and what happens if a payment is missed. None of this is complicated. entertainment.title: M.Inc PR Joins Industry Stakeholders to Explore Africa’s Credit Economy at ACE 2026
entertainment.description: A cross section of industry leaders and stakeholders during the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo 2026 held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. He recalled the influence of teachers who shaped his own experience, particularly Mr. Soewu of Methodist Boys’ High School , whose patience helped students understand difficult concepts without humiliation. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). sports.title: Joe Burrow praises Colbie Young’s work ethic after first NFL touchdown
sports.description: It was an ugly night all-around for the Cincinnati Bengals in Washington, though it did have some bright spots. The weather was part of the ugliness, but the manner in which the Cincinnati Bengals played on Monday Night Football was the remainder of said unsightliness. After slogging to a 10-0 lead, the Bengals appeared to be uninspired for the final two quarters of the game (maybe even more), letting a should-be win slip through their fingers—metaphorically and realistically speaking. Even so, there were a couple of bright spots on an otherwise disappointing evening. After the Commanders tied the game with just under 12 minutes remaining in the third quarter, Cincinnati’s offense was on the move for what would essentially be the last time in the game. Needing a score to try and pull away from Washington’s scrappy efforts, Joe Burrow found rookie Colbie Young for his first touchdown catch as an NFL receiver. Joe Burrow extending the play and finding Colbie Young in the end zone for his first career touchdown reception in the NFL. pic.twitter.com/LVab2j2UZO — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 24, 2026 It was a vintage Burrow play, as he rolled right when the play broke down and found Young in the corner of the end zone. It was a critical play at the time, as the team was largely struggling on offense, and the Bengals regained the lead at 17-10. That was Young’s only catch on two targets against Washington, and only his second on the 2026 season, but it was a gigantic one from an overall game perspective. The Bengals went on to lose, but Young proved to be a bright spot in an otherwise ugly night. And it could be the start of a bigger role moving forward. During his weekly press conference, Burrow made sure to point out Young’s work ethic as part of why he’s growing into his role within the offense. “Seems to never make the same mistake twice. Works hard to be better,” Burrow said of Young. The rookie wide receiver has seen increased snaps with Andrei Iosivas still sitting on injured reserve. And, like Iosivas, Young is in that third receiver role that attempts to clear out space for Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, while also being a blocker in the run game, and occasionally being called upon in the explosive offense. While he’s still growing in the role, this first touchdown reception gives optimism about his development. When the Bengals drafted him in the third round this year, they knew that he was a height/weight/speed/athleticism specimen who could stretch the field but needed polish. The fact that Young’s touchdown reception was a short-yardage one in the red zone on a broken play should catch the attention of the staff. We will see how that ends up translating down the stretch.

Instead, it appears to have galvanised the team, with the Steelers securing a big win over the Denver Broncos. Despite the football game going on, Rodgers remained the biggest talking point, with some Steelers fans voicing their thoughts about their former quarterback with a chant that is unlikely to go down well within the Rodgers household. Pittsburgh Steelers fans vent anger with Aaron Rodgers chant vs Broncos Although the season had by no means been a disaster, it was apparent that something was not right between Rodgers and Mike McCarthy. However, no one would have expected how this week would have panned out, with fans allowing their frustrations with Rodgers to be known. “F*** you, Rodgers,” fans were heard singing on Amazon Prime’s broadcast of the game inside the fourth quarter. However, there is also a clear feeling that Rodgers wanted to drag the Steelers organisation down with him. Even if he was to air out the dirty laundry, perhaps he could have waited until the offseason to do his interview with Pat McAfee. In true Rodgers style, that was not the case, with the 42-year-old looking set to end his NFL career covered in as much controversy as possible. Rodgers has been labelled a bully by some fans, and these Steelers fans in attendance on Friday certainly voiced their thoughts. sports.title: ‘Cannot interact like…’ – Skip Bayless lashes out at Luka Doncic’s courtside altercation with fans
sports.description: Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images Skip Bayless has delivered a strong verdict on Luka Doncic’s interaction with the San Antonio Spurs fans after the game. Luka Doncic’s night ended in disappointment after the Los Angeles Lakers succumbed to a 99-96 loss against their closest Western Conference rivals on Friday night. His abysmal three-point shooting was a big factor in the loss, and the negativity was compounded by what happened after the game. While making his way off the court, Luka ended up in an altercation with two fans. The Slovenian star threw his wristband into the crowd, and then got shoved by a fan after he went back to retrieve it after they said something. The incident caused a lot of commotion on social media, and now Skip Bayless has spoken candidly about it. Skip Bayless says Luka Doncic should not behave in this manner with NBA fans Doncic’s stellar start to the season has seen Bayless, one of his biggest detractors, claim that he has been ‘won over’ by the Lakers superstar. However, the last few games have seen Luka slump, and with this latest fan interaction, Bayless seems far from happy with the Slovenian. After the video of Doncic’s exchange with the fan went viral, the talking head was quick to post on X about how he thinks that Luka should have known better than to do that. “Looked like a man and woman objected to how hard Luka threw her his (I think) wristband. When they said something Luka stormed back, snatched it back, man pushed him. Luka cannot interact like that with fans,” Skip said about the situation. Doncic gave a succinct explanation when asked about his side of the story. The star is naturally more focused on the loss and his own 14-of-31 performance than on this particular moment. sports.title: Real Madrid’s 17-year-old defensive gem shines at U17 World Cup after switching Spain for France
sports.description: Real Madrid’s 17-year-old defensive gem shines at U17 World Cup after switching Spain for France Real Madrid’s next generation is beginning to take shape, with the academy producing a number of gems who have genuine first-team prospects. Los Blancos have placed a lot of emphasis on developing talent in the academy, even if not all players go on to make it to the first team. While players like Thiago Pitarch earn first-team opportunities at the Santiago Bernabeu , others, like Nico Paz and Jacobo Ramon, are sold for significant sums. Now, according to MARCA , another Los Blancos academy prospect, Leo Lemaitre, has been one of the standout defenders at the U-17 World Cup in Qatar. The teenager switched allegiance to represent France rather than Spain and has impressed at the tournament. Leo Lemaitre impressing with France Lemaitre joined Real Madrid at 12 and has steadily climbed through the ranks at La Fabrica over the years. View this post on Instagram A post shared by @leolemaxx He signed a contract extension until 2028 in January and trained with Castilla during pre-season. He has since become part of the Juvenil A set-up. Having made six appearances for Spain’s U-15s and two for the U-16s, the teenager has now switched allegiance to France. His French father, Nicolas, explained that the family maintained close ties to the country, prompting Leo to make the switch. France Under-17 coach Jose Alcocer admitted that the youngster had been difficult to identify because he played outside France and had previously used his mother’s surname. However, the decision already seems to be paying off, with Leo forming an excellent partnership with Mohamed Sylla. Real Madrid have another promising defensive talent The 17-year-old’s numbers in the tournament have been impressive. He is averaging 7.87 ball recoveries per match. Leo has also completed 92% of his passes and 77% of his long balls, showcasing his composure with the ball at his feet. Having a central defender who is comfortable on the ball is important in modern-day football. Jose Mourinho’s immense trust in Dean Huijsen is an example of how much he values composure on the ball. Lemaitre has shown in the tournament that he is good not only at winning the ball back but also at playing it forward. While talk of a potential first-team spot may be premature, his talent is obvious. If his development matches his potential, Real Madrid may have a special player on their hands, and it remains to be seen how Lemaitre fares in the coming seasons.

While Dillingham indeed pushed him first, the Wizards rookie throwing a punch overshadowed that, and it could cost him future NBA opportunities. sports.title: Five of the Premier League's greatest loan cult heroes
sports.description: Five of the Premier League's greatest loan cult heroes Football fans are told never to fall in love with a loan player. But when a temporary transfer produces performances of such quality, it's almost impossible for them not to win hearts. Ronald Araujo is the latest loanee to become a fan favourite, with the defender earning Anfield admiration at Liverpool. Should the Reds opt against a permanent deal, Araujo could join the long list of Premier League loan cult heroes. Carlos Tevez - West Ham Carlos Tevez 's move to West Ham remains one of the most infamous deals in Premier League history. West Ham's shock swoop for the Argentine forward and compatriot Javier Mascherano stunned football, as two of world football's best up-and-coming talents headed to the East End. While Mascherano muddled through a forgettable six months before leaving, Tevez dug deep to make an impact. After a slow start, the forward's form caught fire. He scored his first goal in March, and ended the season with seven goals in nine games. West Ham had been 10 points from safety in early March, but a remarkable run carried the club to safety. Tevez's winner at Manchester United on the final day confirmed Premier League status, and cemented him as a West Ham hero. However, the deal proved controversial. West Ham were found to have breached third-party ownership regulations, with the rights to both Tevez and Mascherano partially held by agent Kia Joorabchian's company, Media Sports Investment (MSI). A messy fallout followed, with Sheffield United, who were relegated at West Ham's expense, eventually receiving £20m in an out-of-court settlement in 2009. Henrik Larsson - Manchester United Manchester United signed Henrik Larsson on a short-term loan deal in 2007, as the Swedish striker arrived to add depth to Sir Alex Ferguson's squad. Larsson had turned down approaches from the Premier League during a decorated career at Celtic, where he scored 242 goals in 313 appearances. In the latter stages of his career, a call from United saw him head to England. He scored three times in 13 appearances, but his impact extended far beyond goals. "In his last game at Middlesbrough, we were winning 2-1 and Henrik went back to play in midfield and ran his balls off," Ferguson wrote in his autobiography. "On his return to the dressing room, all the players stood up and applauded him, and the staff joined in. It takes some player to make that kind of impact in two months. "Cult status can vanish in two minutes if a player isn't doing his job. Yet Henrik retained that aura in his time with us. He looked a natural Man United player, with his movement and courage." Larsson returned to Sweden after his loan, and later admitted an extension was perhaps his only career regret. "That's the only regret I have in my career," Larsson told FourFourTwo . sports.title: NFL fans divided over what Jason Whitlock has said about Aaron Rodgers after Steelers game
sports.description: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images The post-Aaron Rodgers era got off to a surprisingly positive start for the Pittsburgh Steelers, who secured a win over the previously 8-2 Denver Broncos on Friday night. Mason Rudolph is the man tasked with filling Rodgers’ boots and despite not playing 10 or more games in a season since 2019, he played fairly well during the Week 12 action. The Steelers ended up winning 27-5 and on the back of that victory, Jason Whitlock took to X to say that the veteran quarterback made the ‘ultimate sacrifice for his teammates’ and ‘took the bullet to improve the Steelers’. Jason Whitlock says Aaron Rodgers ‘made the ultimate sacrifice’ for the Steelers He wrote: “Aaron Rodgers made the ultimate sacrifice for his teammates. Media won’t give him credit. But Rodgers took the bullet to improve the Steelers.” Some fans have since backed the sentiment expressed by Whitlock, including one who wrote: “This is correct. Took courage to do that too.” Another claimed: “Yep, it is actually remarkable what he did for this team.” “Yep a lot of people know what’s up regardless of the propaganda,” commented a third. However, there were a number of fans who very much disagreed with Whitlock. One suggested: “Aaron Rodgers has never done anything that’s not for his benefit. Never mistake Aaron Rodgers for anything other than Aaron Rodgers’ biggest fan.” “Rodgers never does anything for anyone else,” echoed a second. Another tweeted: “He never did something for other people. It’s always about himself.” A fourth added: “I agree with most of your posts, but not on this.” While fans are no doubt pleased to see their team winning after switching quarterback, it remains to be seen if Rudolph can carry them to the postseason. Against the Broncos he had a 60.0 completion rate, 142 passing yards and averaged 9.5 yards per pass. Meanwhile, before he was let go, Rodgers’ average completion rate in 2026 was 60.9, he was averaging 224.1 passing yards per game and 6.2 yards per pass. While Rudolph did not exactly outshine him in his first start, the change may have had a positive effect on the locker room given there should, at least on paper, be less of a negative atmosphere now. Indeed, both Marc Bernal and Alejandro Balde did not take part in the group session and are major doubts for the trip to Riazor tomorrow. Meanwhile, Fermin Lopez will also miss the game due to his two-match suspension for his red card in the win over Villarreal. Orian Goren trains with Barcelona first team Given that Fermin is unavailable and Bernal is also unlikely to travel, Hansi Flick called up a reinforcement in the midfield department from the reserve team in the form of Orian Goren, reports Mundo Deportivo . Orian Goren trained with the first team. (Picture courtesy: Instagram/@orian_goren) Indeed, the 17-year-old La Masia midfielder took part in the final group training session with the Barcelona first team before their trip to face Deportivo, suggesting that he could be called up to the squad by Flick. A promising young midfield prospect, Goren was part of the senior team’s pre-season preparations under the German tactician and has since been involved in training sessions fairly regularly. In fact, the teenage starlet has even been named in the matchday squad by Flick for two games this season – against Real Madrid and Aston Villa – when Barça were dealing with the absence of Dani Olmo. While he is yet to make his official first-team debut, Goren has played eight times for Juliano Belletti’s Barça Atletic this season, chipping in with a goal and two assists. Orian Goren could be called up vs Deportivo. (Picture courtesy: Instagram/@orian_goren) Now, there is a possibility that the teenage academy product could be on the trip to A Coruna to face Deportivo tomorrow at Riazor. Contract renewal plans underway Goren is currently contracted with Barcelona until the summer of 2028. But as reported earlier this month , the club are already working on a new deal for the young midfielder. Manager Flick is a big admirer of his talents and wants to keep him and Ebrima Tunkara in the first-team dynamics on a regular basis. Having played a part in the Joan Gamper Trophy match during the summer, the 17-year-old is eagerly looking forward to hi official senior debut, while a renewal might soon follow suit.
